Issued at 1232 AM EST Tue Nov 10 2026

             -----------Synoptic Overview-----------

The weather pattern near Florida has changed little over the last
24 hours. A weak subtropical jet extends from Texas to Georgia,
south of a quasi-zonal polar jet passing over the Northern U.S. The
air is still quite dry, especially from 850-700 mb. Slightly higher
moisture resides near and offshore of Southwest Florida.

A ripple of energy in the subtropical jet is still expected to eject
from Texas into the Southeast later today through Wednesday. The
jet stream configuration will become slightly more favorable for
synoptic-scale lift during this period. Some of the moisture just
southwest of the area is forecast to move northward over the next
48 hours, but guidance still disagrees on overall moisture return
and available instability on Wednesday.

The ingredients remain in place for the well-advertised pattern
change late this week. As blocking develops over the northern
latitudes of N America, significant amplification of the longwave
pattern will begin late on Wednesday. Eventually, a deep trough will
gather over the Eastern U.S. by Thursday. A vigorous shortwave
digging through the developing trough will promote surface
cyclogenesis over the Ohio Valley. As the low moves toward the
Delmarva Peninsula, it is expected to force a strong cold front
toward Florida. The front should arrive late Thursday and pass
the entire district by Friday morning.

Ensembles are in excellent agreement with pattern evolution through
at least Saturday, when PWAT (moisture) values fall to 30-50% of
normal and 925 mb temperatures dip to +6 to +10 deg C. This will
represent the most significant continental air mass intrusion into
the Florida Peninsula so far this autumn.

Guidance slowly moves the large trough eastward this weekend,
with the lowest 500 mb heights moving off the Northeast U.S. coast
by late Sunday. Surface high pressure will follow in its wake,
its center remaining well north of Florida. Once the high moves
east of our longitude, onshore flow should redevelop on Sunday,
allowing temperature moderation to begin.

Guidance quickly breaks down the high-latitude block next week,
allowing the flow to become progressive across the U.S. Therefore,
the upcoming cooldown this weekend is not expected to last long, and
unsettled weather also may not wait too long to return. For example,
just yesterday the ECMWF-AIFS ensemble was nearly alone with its
indication of another shortwave within the subtropical jet reaching
the northern Gulf in about a week. Cluster analysis now reveals
that nearly half of physics-based members support this solution.

             -------Sensible Weather & Impacts-------

Today - Tonight...

Status-quo weather is favored for most of us on this Tuesday. Aside
from some patchy morning fog, we expect partly sunny and warm
weather today with highs in the low to mid 80s. Beaches will still
be a concern, as the lingering swell continues to produce a high
risk of numerous rip currents. Please stay out of the ocean.

With subtle moisture return expected over South Florida today,
we have introduced a small (20%) chance of showers near Lake
Okeechobee this afternoon and evening. Most areas will stay dry
through tonight, however.

Wednesday - Thursday night...

We'll be keeping an eye on a disturbance approaching from the Gulf
on Wednesday. Moisture will be increasing a bit, but the extent is
in question, with significant disagreement in the guidance. This
adds up to a 20-40% chance of afternoon and early evening showers
and storms, with the highest coverage along the coast south of Cape
Canaveral. A few models, led by the ECMWF, have ample instability
in place. Others, such as the HRRR, are more stable. With moderate
effective shear profiles, there is a conditional chance of a strong
storm Wednesday afternoon. Gusty winds of 45-50 mph and coin-sized
hail would be the primary hazards.

On Thursday, breezy westerly winds are forecast to develop, with
drier air mixing to the surface in the afternoon. Only isolated
shower chances persist through Thursday night, and mostly over our
southern communities. Rainfall amounts through Thursday night look
rather light, with only a 1-in-10 chance of exceeding a half inch
along the coast from Melbourne southward.

The strong cold front will not arrive until Thursday night. Despite
more cloud cover, highs on Wednesday should reach the low to mid
80s with upper 70s to low 80s on Thursday.

Friday - Weekend...

With the cold front quickly marching off to our south, winds
turn northwesterly on Friday and Saturday and stay breezy from
time to time. This will usher cooler and drier air into the area,
with the coolest air arriving early Saturday.

Under clearing skies, highs on Friday should range from the upper
60s to low 70s, but dip on Saturday into the mid to upper 60s. Lows
